findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly what the automated must-block/must-pass regression tests assert: fix the deterministic boundary (e.g. tests assert DET-floor block + candidate forwarding into the fenced context via the fake screen verdict map; the REAL verifier disposition rule block/pass per fixture is proven only by the AC10 operator-attested live run), so no automated test depends on live-verifier LLM judgment.
evidence: 'All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map (deterministic, no live model)' — names only the screen, not the verifier
AC5: 'blocks only undispositioned deliverable-defects per the store-grounded disposition rule ... (verified by the must-block/must-pass regression fixtures)'
The verifier adjudication is an LLM judgment (completion_verifier.md); a deterministic automated assertion of block/pass requires either faking the verifier or the operator-attested run

AC10 [operator-attested] already carries '(ii) the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture through the REAL disposition rule' — implying the automated path does NOT prove the real verifier disposition
findings.finding: The plan states all automated regression tests drive the SCREEN through a fake forced-choice verdict map, but leaves unspecified whether the VERIFIER's adjudication (the actual block/pass decision the must-block/must-pass fixtures assert) is faked or live in those automated tests. The verifier is itself an LLM (completion_verifier.md); if it is not faked, the automated must-block/must-pass tests are non-deterministic and cannot be a proving command; if it IS faked, then AC5's disposition rule (store-grounded a/b signals) is only actually exercised by the operator-attested live run, and the automated tests prove only DET floor + forwarding plumbing.
findings.location: Testing section ('drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map') vs AC line 5 ('verified by the must-block/must-pass regression fixtures') and AC line 8
scenarios: CI runs the must-block regression for 30a2/5b09 and the outcome depends on live LLM verifier judgment (flaky)
A reviewer credits AC5 as proven by automated tests when the disposition rule is only actually validated by the manual calibration run
findings.suggested_fix: In the Testing section, add: 'Automated tests fake BOTH the screen verdict map AND stub the verifier decision path (or assert only up to the forwarded candidate block); the verifier's real store-grounded block/pass per fixture is validated exclusively by the AC10 operator-attested calibration run, so no CI test depends on live LLM judgment.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate in Scope the DET-floor ENFORCEMENT edit to the completion_precheck op (gate_ops.py): on a detected open/in_progress caused_by subtree bug, short-circuit exactly like the unclosed-child gate (run_verify=False + deterministic FAIL verdict with the teaching message, ELSE/passthrough arm), distinct from the candidate-context append.
evidence: Plan: 'DET floor: ... = deterministic block (like the direct-children gate, completion.py ~:90)'
Plan Scope: 'gate_ops.py (completion_precheck: append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change)' — no mention of the floor short-circuit

Code: gate_ops.py:63-74 shows the direct-children gate's block is a run_verify=False + deterministic FAIL verdict returned FROM completion_precheck, and completion-verification.yaml:37-38 branches on steps.precheck.outputs.run_verify — so 'like the direct-children gate' requires an analogous edit to completion_precheck
completion.py:388 verify_completion delegates verdict production to the workflow, so the floor cannot block from completion.py alone
findings.finding: The DET caused_by floor's ENFORCEMENT (the deterministic short-circuit BLOCK that skips the LLM, analogous to the direct-children gate) must be wired into the completion_precheck op in gate_ops.py — the same place the unclosed-child short-circuit lives (gate_ops.py:63-74, returning run_verify=False + a FAIL verdict so the ELSE/passthrough arm is taken) — but the plan's Scope entry for gate_ops.py names ONLY 'append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change', and the completion.py entry names only the floor detection + candidate filter. The floor's block-wiring in completion_precheck is left unenumerated.
findings.location: Scope: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py and src/rebar/llm/completion.py entries; Approach stage 1
scenarios: An open caused_by bug in the subtree exists at epic close: the floor must set run_verify=False and emit a FAIL verdict from completion_precheck so the LLM is skipped and close is blocked — but the plan's gate_ops.py scope only covers context injection, so the block seam is un-scoped.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the gate_ops.py Scope bullet to read '(completion_precheck: DET-floor short-circuit BLOCK mirroring the unclosed-child gate — run_verify=False + deterministic FAIL verdict; AND append compact candidates into the fenced context; no output-schema change)', and note in the completion.py bullet that it supplies the floor DETECTION helper consumed by that short-circuit.

findings.finding: The verifier's disposition adjudication (block only an undispositioned deliverable-defect; SATISFY via supersedes/duplicates link or reasoned pre-existence prose) is the core novel behavior that separates the must-block fixtures (30a2, 5b09) from the must-pass fixtures (30d3 prose, e6a0 link, c8ed link) — but the plan states automated tests 'drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map' and the sole live acceptance criterion covers only the screen's A/B/C -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path, not the live verifier's disposition decision over those fixtures. If both the screen verdict and the verifier verdict are faked, the must-block/must-pass regression assertions validate only plumbing while the disposition rule — the riskiest new logic — never runs as it will in production.
findings.location: Testing section ('All regression/unit tests drive the screen through a FAKE forced-choice verdict map ... the live haiku path is exercised only in manual calibration runs') and AC line 9 ([operator-attested] live calibration run 'proving the real model -> epic_bug_screen_verdict validator path')
findings.suggested_fix: Add an acceptance criterion that the live calibration run also records the verifier's block/pass outcome per fixture (proving 30d3/e6a0/c8ed pass and 30a2/5b09 block through the real disposition rule), keeping the automated suite on the fake map for the screen only.

evidence: 3 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The disposition-rule signal (a) — 'a supersedes or duplicates LINK (either direction) connecting the bug to the epic subtree or to a named successor ticket' — is inconsistent with the plan's own fixture mapping and misses the common prose-supersession case: fixture e6a0-ba9b records its supersession as a COMMENT ('Superseded by epic 4702-a55c-7aeb-445a…') and carries NO supersedes/duplicates link in its deps (only relates_to→5fd2), yet the plan asserts 'e6a0 satisfies via (a)'. By contrast c8ed-d52d does carry a real supersedes→ecc7 link, so it genuinely satisfies via (a). As specified, e6a0 can only satisfy via signal (b) (reasoned prose), so an implementer encoding the stated mapping ('e6a0 satisfies via (a)') would write a regression assertion that cannot hold against the store, and the link-based signal (a) will systematically fail to recognize dispositions recorded as prose rather than as a graph edge.
findings.location: Approach, stage-3 disposition rule + 'Fixture mapping' clause; Testing (must-pass e6a0-ba9b 'disposition trail: filed then superseded by epic 4702')
findings.suggested_fix: Reclassify e6a0 as a signal-(b) fixture (substantive supersession prose in a comment) and keep c8ed as the signal-(a) fixture; add an explicit note that a supersession recorded only as prose is intentionally handled by (b), not (a).
